modules.title: Simple moving average
modules.learn: The SMA summarizes the last N completed closes. A close above it is contextual evidence, not an automatic buy signal.
modules.question: With five completed prices, changing the lookback changes the average; which conclusion is justified?
options: A crossover confirms guaranteed follow-through.
You must declare the period and bar completion before interpreting SMA.
A single SMA level reveals whether institutions are buying.
modules.feedback: The average depends on the chosen lookback and completed prices. The indicator lags, and crossovers can fail.
modules.transferQuestion: A bar touches SMA during a choppy session. What should the learner check?
transferOptions: Treat the touch as guaranteed support.
Confirm structure, volume scope, and risk before considering a setup.
Assume the candle finishes at its current high.
modules.transferFeedback: The new context requires independent price structure and risk evidence; an SMA touch alone cannot qualify entry.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.

modules.title: Exponential moving average
modules.learn: The EMA gives newer prices greater weight; its speed depends on period and seeding.
modules.question: Two EMA settings cross in a choppy market. What does the event establish?
options: The averages changed relative position but may whipsaw.
A profit is statistically guaranteed.
The next candle must close higher.
modules.feedback: A crossover states a relationship between two smoothed series. It has no guaranteed predictive outcome.
modules.transferQuestion: EMA9 rises but price loses a predeclared swing level. Which matters?
transferOptions: The EMA cancels invalidation.
The recorded swing invalidation still governs the scenario.
Only EMA9 can set the holding horizon.
modules.transferFeedback: A derivative indicator does not override an independent risk or structure veto.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.

modules.title: Relative strength index
modules.learn: RSI compares smoothed average price gains with losses. High RSI can persist during strong trends.
modules.question: RSI is above 70 on the available bars. What can Talia conclude?
options: Price must reverse on the next bar.
RSI shows strong recent upward momentum; overbought is not a timing guarantee.
A short order will fill at its planned stop.
modules.feedback: Wilder RSI summarizes momentum; an extreme reading cannot independently predict when reversal occurs.
modules.transferQuestion: RSI is 32 in a continuing downtrend. What is the defensible interpretation?
transferOptions: A bounce is certain.
The oscillator is low but the structure and invalidation still matter.
Low RSI means the seller is an institution.
modules.transferFeedback: Oversold is context, not an observable completed reversal.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.

modules.title: Moving average convergence divergence
modules.learn: MACD compares faster and slower price EMAs; the histogram is MACD minus its signal line.
modules.question: The MACD histogram crosses above zero. What does this prove?
options: The MACD line is above its signal line under declared settings.
A position must be entered now.
The stock is cheaper than its intrinsic value.
modules.feedback: It describes indicator relationships under a period/seed setting, not a validated profitable entry.
modules.transferQuestion: MACD improves while the trade's risk level breaks. Which judgment is sound?
transferOptions: Hold because momentum is positive.
Reassess because the original invalidation was reached.
MACD eliminates slippage.
modules.transferFeedback: The documented risk condition cannot be erased by a correlated indicator.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.

modules.title: Average true range
modules.learn: ATR averages true ranges that account for prior-close gaps; it measures magnitude, not direction.
modules.question: A bar gaps above the preceding close. Which value belongs in true range?
options: Only current high minus low.
The maximum of high-low, high-prior close, and low-prior close absolute distances.
The current close minus opening price.
modules.feedback: True range captures gap effects that a simple high-low measure can miss.
modules.transferQuestion: ATR doubles after a volatility shock. What changes in a plan?
transferOptions: Predicted price direction is now certain.
Volatility and possible risk-distance assumptions need review.
Liquidity and spreads are guaranteed to improve.
modules.transferFeedback: ATR estimates historic movement size, not directional probability or executable stop fills.
modules.scope: Fictional one-minute OHLCV bars and deterministic calculation; no future candle in a visible indicator value, no validated strategy.

modules.title: Bollinger bands
modules.learn: Bands display a moving average plus/minus a selected standard-deviation multiple. Touches do not prove reversals.
modules.question: Price touches the upper Bollinger band. What is a defensible observation?
options: Price is high relative to this rolling band, not necessarily ready to fall.
A sell at the band is mandatory.
The band guarantees 95% success.
modules.feedback: Band contact is location and volatility context, not a probability promise.
modules.transferQuestion: The bands narrow during consolidation. What does this tell the learner?
transferOptions: Low recent band-measured dispersion; breakout direction remains unconfirmed.
The next move must be upward.
The watchlist is automatically trade-qualified.
modules.transferFeedback: Compression can change risk context but does not dictate future direction.

modules.title: Volume weighted average price
modules.learn: This visualization uses bar HLC3 weighted by volume, an explicit approximation of actual transaction VWAP.
modules.question: Displayed bar-based VWAP rises while price crosses it. What is the right limitation?
options: The displayed proxy is not a venue-exact tick VWAP and a cross needs context.
The proxy identifies institutional order identities.
Any crossing guarantees a profitable continuation.
modules.feedback: The bar proxy is a learning calculation; feed, session and anchor decisions change its meaning.
modules.transferQuestion: A premarket VWAP and regular-session VWAP disagree. What must be checked?
transferOptions: Choose whichever best fits the later outcome.
State session inclusions and anchor before comparison.
Average both without considering timestamps.
modules.transferFeedback: Anchors and feed scope must be reconciled before drawing a conclusion.

modules.title: Relative volume
modules.learn: Relative volume compares observed share quantity to a declared historical baseline, ideally the same clock time.
modules.question: At 10:00, 600,000 shares versus a matched-time baseline 200,000 shares yields RVOL 3.0. What does it prove?
options: Activity is three times this baseline, not whether buyers will win.
The stock will gain 3%.
A chart entry is confirmed automatically.
modules.feedback: RVOL measures activity relative to the denominator; directional thesis and execution require independent checks.
modules.transferQuestion: A platform compares 10:00 volume to full-day average. What is the issue?
transferOptions: No issue, the denominator is identical.
The clock windows differ and can distort the comparison.
The count proves a short squeeze.
modules.transferFeedback: Time-matched and full-session denominators are distinct metrics.

modules.title: Discovery is not trade qualification
modules.learn: Discovery → research → watch → qualifying trigger → risk review. A scanner hit never proves a completed entry setup.
modules.question: A fictional symbol passes the scanner but its five-minute confirmation bar is unfinished. What state fits?
options: ENTER immediately.
WATCH / WAIT until the declared trigger completes.
Award a graded competency pass.
modules.feedback: Discovery does not establish entry confirmation or executable liquidity.
modules.transferQuestion: A candidate later jumps 12% after a NO TRADE decision. Was the earlier decision necessarily wrong?
transferOptions: Yes, all later winners had to be bought.
No, judge the original available evidence and risk vetoes.
Change the original timestamp.
modules.transferFeedback: A valid watchlist judgment requires a timestamp, known source, explicit filters, risk vetoes, and separation of discovery from entry.
modules.scope: Fictional four-candidate scan, no live exchange quotes, broker orders, or current watchlist persistence.

modules.title: Premarket candidate verification
modules.learn: Separate premarket trades, regular-hours opening auction, corporate-action adjustments, spread and verified catalyst publication.
modules.question: A large premarket gap lacks a verified issuer filing and has a wide spread. What follows?
options: Qualified breakout trade.
RESEARCH / WAIT with explicit missing evidence.
Guaranteed opening continuation.
modules.feedback: An impressive gap is discovery; source and liquidity checks remain required.
modules.transferQuestion: A reverse split makes an unadjusted premarket gap appear dramatic. What next?
transferOptions: Reconcile adjusted prices and share identity.
Use raw chart highs from any date.
Treat the split as strong earnings.
modules.transferFeedback: A valid watchlist judgment requires a timestamp, known source, explicit filters, risk vetoes, and separation of discovery from entry.

modules.title: Matched-clock volume filters
modules.learn: Require same-clock cumulative volume comparisons with explicit historical session and sampling rules.
modules.question: RVOL 3.0 appears from 10:00-to-full-day comparison. What is the risk?
options: No risk, all denominators are equivalent.
The denominator mismatch may overstate or understate unusual trading.
A bullish entry is guaranteed.
modules.feedback: Use comparable elapsed periods and data scope; do not turn volume into direction.
modules.transferQuestion: Matched-time RVOL is high but quote spread fails the threshold. What now?
transferOptions: Hard liquidity veto still applies.
High RVOL replaces quote checks.
Ignore the bid/ask.
modules.transferFeedback: A valid watchlist judgment requires a timestamp, known source, explicit filters, risk vetoes, and separation of discovery from entry.

modules.title: Spread and depth veto
modules.learn: Use quoted spread and time-stamped depth alongside realized activity; volume totals do not promise execution.
modules.question: Scanner signal is strong but spread exceeds the written maximum. What is justified?
options: Hard NO TRADE for that setup.
Entry because three indicators agree.
Assume the spread will vanish at fill.
modules.feedback: Execution risk is a hard gate, not a soft score. A wide quoted spread can invalidate a planned entry despite favorable technical signals; verify liquidity and potential slippage before promoting the candidate.
modules.transferQuestion: A displayed ask contains only 200 shares and planned size is 1,000. What can be assumed?
transferOptions: Full order fills at one displayed ask price.
Nothing about the whole fill price; book may change.
A stop guarantees loss ceiling.
modules.transferFeedback: A valid watchlist judgment requires a timestamp, known source, explicit filters, risk vetoes, and separation of discovery from entry.

modules.title: Primary-source catalyst queue
modules.learn: Verify company identity, original document and publicly available timestamp before classifying news.
modules.question: An online article is dated after the replay decision timestamp. Can it support the earlier decision?
options: No, publication later cannot justify prior knowledge.
Yes, later news is always known.
Only if the price later rose.
modules.feedback: No-lookahead chronology is more important than hindsight narratives.
modules.transferQuestion: A social post cites earnings but no issuer release is available. What is the state?
transferOptions: Verifiably catalyst-qualified.
VERIFY_PENDING until primary source and time match.
A confirmed market order.

modules.title: Journal rejected candidates
modules.learn: Log the missing condition, actual decision timestamp and subsequent outcome separately; do not grade no-trades by later winners.
modules.question: A stock rallies after you rejected it for a predeclared wide-spread veto. What should be recorded?
options: Rewrite the earlier decision as a mistake.
Keep the original valid veto and analyze the later move separately.
Delete the stop and entry rules.
modules.feedback: The later move is an outcome, not proof that the earlier unsupported entry was justified.
modules.transferQuestion: What documented evidence makes a NO TRADE decision complete and reviewable without hindsight?
transferOptions: A recorded condition, observation time and reason for rejection.
A forecast of guaranteed future loss.
No documentation.
